S06.title: Week 1 Finding Home opening
S06.objective: Recognize that this week's arc is finding a note, following a journey, then placing a moving note over a reference.
S06.how_to_read: Native static sequence labels 'Find C → Travel → Add a voice', plus accurate small C-key landmark below; avoid claiming three-chord theory.
S06.keyboard_action: Explain each stage and point ahead to Lessons 1A/1B/1C; at instrument find one C, play two nearby notes, then briefly sustain C while another note enters if their synth permits.
S06.guard: Build from approved site atmosphere A without poster plate; no site playback or clickable notes.

A01.title: One Note Becomes a Place
A01.placement: 1A after opening real-keyboard setup, before note names
A01.objective: Understand that a played note can be a single stable musical event and that a picture can treat it as a reference.
A01.how_to_read: Native key illustration may show one unlabelled white key being pressed here; simple static annotation: one sound remains, not a chord or an entire scale.
A01.keyboard_action: Teach note as musical sound, listen to one note physically; ask what about it persists when held and how the sound's color might vary with the synth tone.
A01.guard: No pitch-letter prerequisite; metaphor does not scientifically illustrate amplitude or frequency.

A02.title: Pitch versus Loudness
A02.placement: 1A definition of pitch before locating C
A02.objective: Tell apart high/low pitch from loud/soft volume.
A02.how_to_read: Accurate actual neighboring-key example; rightward keyboard position conventionally higher, leftward lower. Labels 'higher/lower' and 'louder/softer' in different native visual axes.
A02.keyboard_action: Describe which action changes pitch (play a more rightward key) and which changes volume (play softer/louder or change volume control); learner tries both on own synth.
A02.guard: Do not ask the model to draw an oscilloscope or incorrect wave amplitude chart; keyboard's grouping deterministic.

A03.title: Find C by Two Black Keys
A03.note: M02 G02 accent reused; narrow layout A03-narrow
A03.placement: 1A first named pitch and keyboard geography
A03.objective: Identify any C as the white key immediately left of each two-black-key group.
A03.how_to_read: Draw full repeating two/three-black-key groups from keyboard geometry, two C highlights, small locator guides, native C labels; no hidden labels, no buttons, accurate E–F and B–C.
A03.keyboard_action: Teach the two-black-key landmark and trace the left-adjacent white key; learner finds and plays multiple Cs on their own instrument.
A03.guard: Keyboard remains a factual static illustration; a 'reveal the Cs' control from M02 pilot must not ship.

A04.title: C as Chosen Home / Concentric Tonal Center
A04.note: approved M02 G01 art reused; new static native labels
A04.placement: 1A after finding C and learning contextual musical reference
A04.objective: See one chosen reference C and the surrounding visiting notes; understand that 'home' depends on music context.
A04.how_to_read: Native C center and named D E F G A B visitor labels and a static correctly positioned return path, plus real C highlight beneath; legible explanation 'relationship map, not to scale'.
A04.keyboard_action: Walk C→D→E then back to C with fingertips on synth; compare a phrase ending at G with one ending at C. Say the white keys alone do NOT prove C is home.
A04.guard: Do not bake letters in model art, claim C drone proves C-major key, infer tone colors objectively.

A05.title: Seven Names, Ordered White-Key Journey
A05.placement: 1A immediately after A03 and before octave
A05.objective: Follow C D E F G A B C in correct order and distinguish white-key order from semitone size.
A05.how_to_read: Exact eight white key positions, repeated higher C, visible E–F/B–C boundaries and no equal-chromatic-semitone implication. Two static layouts for narrow/wide screens.
A05.keyboard_action: Read the letters in sequence while playing consecutive white keys from C to next C, then back. Notice where the black keys do and don't interrupt.
A05.guard: Do not model-render any key or label; the route is visually ordered, not a measured radial spacing.

A06.title: Octave Return Spiral
A06.objective: See that a higher C has the same note name but a genuinely higher pitch.
A06.how_to_read: Two deterministic C keyboard positions separated by one octave; two independent static C labels and an upward pitch-arrow/spiral path registered to art.
A06.keyboard_action: Describe same named family at a new height; learner plays lower then higher C and back, without learner-facing C3/C4/C5 numbering.
A06.guard: Spiral is poetic recurrence, not a calibrated hertz graph; optional 2:1 frequency science belongs in documented enrichment.

A07.title: Ascending and Descending C-to-C
A07.objective: Distinguish going up an octave from returning down using the same note set.
A07.how_to_read: Label direction up/right vs down/left with genuine ordered keys; two static views, not clickable trace.
A07.keyboard_action: Learner plays C to next higher C, then steps back; encourage noticing how the sense of height changes.
A07.guard: Avoid random pitch jumps masquerading as sequential white-key steps.

A08.title: Two Endings: Away and Home
A08.objective: See a path that departs from chosen home and understand the effect of different endpoints.
A08.how_to_read: Exact native educational example(s) shown as clearly authored practice rather than fabricated historical fixture. E.g. same first notes C–D–E, compare ending on G versus C, drawn as two static pathways with labels only after lesson explains comparison.
A08.keyboard_action: Explain that context makes C a reference, but the listener can experience ending points differently; learner plays identical opening twice, finishing once on G and once on C, describes own response.
A08.guard: Early version before any answer-prediction must be neutral; do not universally assign emotions to destinations.

A09.title: Drone: A Note That Stays While Others Visit
A09.placement: 1A introducing sustained reference and visiting note
A09.objective: Understand 'drone' as one continuing held note under changing notes.
A09.how_to_read: Native continuous C foundation label, separate E/G/D educational visitor labels if introduced; if showing actual historical A02 event, verify exact starting and duration from week1 fixtures first. No web-sound control.
A09.keyboard_action: Explain which strand stays and which comes and goes, then sustain C with one hand or sustain pedal while playing one other note; if impossible physically, alternate playing notes and imagining C or use explicitly optional external reference.
A09.guard: One C held is not by itself a full chord or proof of tonic; shapes not sound-wave measurements.

A10.title: Tiny Personal Melody and Pauses
A10.objective: Use a handful of known notes to create a deliberate phrase with a resting point or change.
A10.how_to_read: Native illustrative EXAMPLE melody e.g. C–D–E–C, explicitly marked as example rather than authoritative event fixture, with static keyboard callout and a gap marker; learner may use their own notes.
A10.keyboard_action: Invite learner to make a three/four-note idea, repeat it with a pause or different final note and listen to what changed.
A10.guard: Do not force recording/DAW account or an invented official source recording.

A11.title: Paint What You Hear — Personal Color Map
A11.placement: 1A optional creative door after hands-on melody
A11.objective: Connect own imaginative response to music without treating colors as universal pitch facts.
A11.how_to_read: Native caption 'Your own sound-to-color interpretation' and source-preserved enrichment text; no fixed pitch=color legend.
A11.keyboard_action: Ask learner to play a note on real keyboard and sketch or imagine what the sound resembles, then play another and compare.
A11.guard: Color choices are artistic, not scientific synesthesia.

A12.title: Lesson 1A Recap / Printed Reference
A12.note: recap sheet with ink-light print variant
A12.placement: 1A close, week hub thumbnail and printable
A12.objective: Recall C landmark, white-key path, octave, contextual home and a visiting note.
A12.how_to_read: Panels: 2-black-key C locator, C–C octave path, C-as-chosen-center diagram, held-vs-moving small example; real source labels; no stateful controls.
A12.keyboard_action: Explain one key idea per mini panel. Learner plays a home note and one short journey, then describes the sense of return.
A12.guard: Preserve researched 1A content including tonic/timbre nuance and original optional learning doors in later content integration. ## Lesson 1B

B01.title: Open Ending versus Arrival
B01.note: early answer-neutral page and later pair
B01.objective: See two related endings with shared beginning but different final destination.
B01.how_to_read: Native accurate W1 fixture pair: B01 seven rising upper notes C D E F G A B; B02 adds higher C only. Render early page B01 path alone; later static B01/B02 side-by-side with C final labeled.
B01.keyboard_action: First learner plays C through B and notices open stopping point without seeing the arrival answer; after reading next static page plays higher C afterward and compares.
B01.guard: No interactive reveal or pre-exposure of higher C in first question. Subjective completeness varies.

B02.title: Where Half Steps Really Are
B02.objective: Find a semitone as the immediate neighboring physical key, including white-white E–F and B–C.
B02.how_to_read: Static precise E–F and B–C adjacency, C–C♯ as chromatic neighboring keys, and note group geometry. Label 1 semitone in each case.
B02.keyboard_action: Explain that adjacent keys are always one semitone even if both are white; learner plays C then black key, E then F and B then C.
B02.guard: Do not render black key between E–F or B–C. Do not substitute equal white-key spacing for interval measurement.

B03.title: Whole Step = Two Semitones
B03.objective: Trace two neighboring chromatic key moves to travel a whole step.
B03.how_to_read: Static C→C♯→D (two semitone hops), C→D total 2, also optional E→F♯ and truthful black key. Native endpoint and intermediate key labels.
B03.keyboard_action: Guide the learner to play C, the immediately neighboring black key, then D, and contrast with C straight to D.
B03.guard: Never imply skipping one white key universally equals whole step.

B04.title: One White-Key Move, Two Actual Distances
B04.objective: Compare C→D (2 semitones) with E→F (1) despite both appearing as adjacent white keys.
B04.how_to_read: Native semitone count labels C–D 2, E–F 1; first path crosses C♯, second no black key.
B04.keyboard_action: Teach why the keyboard's repeating black groups matter; learner plays and counts both journeys.
B04.guard: Correct counterexample B–C=1 may be added as side key strip.

B05.title: Major Scale: Unequal Step Garland
B05.objective: See one coherent scale with intentional unequal step sizes, not arbitrary seven equal segments.
B05.how_to_read: Draw accurate static C D E F G A B C with measured semitone hop pattern W W H W W W H (2,2,1,2,2,2,1); native keyboard and classifying labels. Generated petal distances artistic only; a separate native ruler proves the count.
B05.keyboard_action: Walk the major scale with keyboard, noticing E–F and B–C half steps; try from a different pitch only as optional curiosity with physical guidance.
B05.guard: Do not assign petal width quantitative meaning unless native measured overlay specifically enforces it.

B06.title: Seven Names and Next C
B06.objective: Connect seven named notes and the repeating upper C to the scale.
B06.how_to_read: Native sequence C D E F G A B C and two distinct C key positions; optional W/W/H ruler in later-step version.
B06.keyboard_action: Learner plays up and down, locating the return C by two-black-key landmark.
B06.guard: Do not commission new center mandala when A05/A06/B05 suffice.

B07.title: Answer-Neutral Unfinished Path
B07.note: = B01-early; answer-neutral, no higher C anywhere
B07.placement: 1B FIRST prediction page before showing ending
B07.objective: Invite learner to imagine a possible ending without exposing the source's higher-C resolution.
B07.how_to_read: Native seven notes C D E F G A B only. Do NOT show the source B02 C5 in early legend/alt text or the earlier step.
B07.keyboard_action: Learner plays the seven notes, pauses and imagines a next note; turn page to see an example choice and compare.
B07.guard: Protect existing expectation/reveal-before-answer sequence without a button or quiz.

B08.title: Same Beginning / Different Last Note
B08.objective: Make the difference in last note explicit while holding the beginning constant.
B08.how_to_read: Native shared C D E F G A B, only arrival includes higher C; optional learner-created alternative last note labelled as independent exercise.
B08.keyboard_action: Learner plays two endings and describes their own auditory response; encourage making a third distinct ending.
B08.guard: Do not assert universal closure/unfinished emotion from any interval.

B09.title: Closeness versus Measured Distance
B09.objective: Understand that physical keyboard spacing/semitone count and conceptual feeling of closeness are different kinds of information.
B09.how_to_read: Native exact side-by-side C–C♯ 1 semitone and C–D 2 semitones ruler on real keyboard; explain art arcs are conceptual.
B09.keyboard_action: Ask learner to play neighboring keys then a whole step, listening for how the relationship changes.
B09.guard: Do not use circle radius as a quantitative semitone rule.

B10.title: Make Your Own Arrival and Open Ending
B10.objective: Design two short musical choices from one shared beginning.
B10.how_to_read: Native example stem C D E if needed with separate static endpoint examples; explain these are authored practice patterns, not lesson source fixture unless matched.
B10.keyboard_action: Create two mini melodies on keyboard with same first notes and different end; notice which better serves learner's own idea.
B10.guard: Do not introduce DAW, a virtual keyboard, answer-checking or sound buttons.

B11.title: Why the Major-Scale Pattern Travels
B11.note: optional enrichment; G-major pattern asserted in code
B11.objective: Grasp that a step pattern, not key color, defines the major scale, and different starting notes can need black keys.
B11.how_to_read: Native C-major WWHWWWH. An alternate key example must be calculated/verified and explicitly introduced as enrichment, not an unverified screenshot.
B11.keyboard_action: Try beginning on another familiar key and noting when black keys appear; optional exploration without requiring full theory.
B11.guard: Don't force more advanced key signatures into beginner lesson. ## Lesson 1C

C01.title: The Held Foundation with Visiting Upper Notes
C01.objective: See harmony as two independent voices, one continuous and one visiting.
C01.how_to_read: Native static source 1C C01 lower C held 0–12s; upper E 2–4s, G 5–7s, D 9–11s; if native time ruler shown, exact event lengths above; no model timing labels.
C01.keyboard_action: Explain voice as independent musical line and simultaneous notes as harmony; learner sustains C and alternates E G D if physically feasible.
C01.guard: Do not insist C+E is a triad; no audio playback.

C02.title: Two Distinct Voices — One Scene
C02.objective: Distinguish a stable foundation from independent upper melody even when both sound together.
C02.how_to_read: Native lower/upper voice labels anchored at appropriate points with accurate source example C01 and separate faint keyboard positions.
C02.keyboard_action: Point out that each color/strand represents a voice and there can be overlapping pitches; learner tries each line separately on own instrument then combines if able.
C02.guard: Do not encode extra fictitious notes or let color alone carry voice identities.

C03.title: Lower and Higher Voice Positions
C03.objective: Locate lower C and higher E/G/D correctly on the real keyboard.
C03.how_to_read: Native key positions C lower, E/G/D upper for C01 fixture; label as 'lower voice' and 'upper voice' with distinct line/shape conventions.
C03.keyboard_action: Read the map, play the lower key then upper and notice pitch height independent of hand position.
C03.guard: Do not draw keys via image model; learner-facing numerical octave labels unnecessary.

C04.title: Early versus Late Entrance
C04.objective: See that the same note entering at a different time changes a phrase's shape even when pitch remains.
C04.how_to_read: Native timing labels from C02: E 2–6s over C 0–12; C03: E 7–11s over C 0–12. Both upper notes E at same pitch, only onset differs.
C04.keyboard_action: Explain entrance, duration and silence; learner sustains C then plays E early and late in separate versions, noticing the change.
C04.guard: Do not use animation or click-to-compare; both examples static on one lesson page.

C05.title: Time as a Musical Relationship
C05.objective: Read horizontal time and distinguish held note, entrance, rest and change.
C05.how_to_read: Exact start/end times for chosen 1C source fixture; draw no time marks in the model output.
C05.keyboard_action: Lead reader from the lower continuous bar to timed upper marks; learner recreates the sequence slowly on keyboard or taps a steady pulse before playing.
C05.guard: Timeline is measured; decorative colored swirls never substitute for accurate timed positions.

C06.title: One Voice Alone, Then Both Together
C06.placement: 1C compare isolated roles conceptually without playback
C06.objective: Understand that two voices can be heard separately and together while keeping their roles.
C06.how_to_read: Same source C01 event paths in all three panels, hiding none behind controls. Exact note-event membership maintained.
C06.keyboard_action: Play C alone, melodic E/G/D separately, then try both on own instrument; notice how the total sound changes.

C07.title: The Same 36 Seconds, Two Endings
C07.placement: 1C late lesson comparison after starting material learned
C07.objective: Recognize a shared musical journey but two distinct final possibilities.
C07.how_to_read: Native 1C C04/C05 shared C 0–36s and upper E (8–12), G (15–19), D (23–27), B (29–32); only C04 adds upper C 33–35.8s. If there is an expectation prompt, compare only on later static step.
C07.keyboard_action: Walk the shared four notes and final difference, then play two final options on real keyboard; listener decides how each works.
C07.guard: Do not show final C on an earlier prediction page; source timings verified.

C08.title: Silence as Compositional Space
C08.objective: Perceive gaps and waiting as purposeful elements of a two-voice idea.
C08.how_to_read: Native annotation 'upper voice rests' at source C01 gaps, exact timing only if charted separately; no fake waveform.
C08.keyboard_action: Learner plays a short idea with one pause; repeats without pause and notices different pacing.
C08.guard: Silence in upper line is not total silence if lower foundation continues.

C09.title: Compose a Two-Voice Story
C09.objective: Plan a stable base, a short melody, a meaningful pause, a change and an ending.
C09.how_to_read: Native headings set a scene → imagine visitor → leave room → change something → choose ending; sample keyboard labels drawn from already taught notes.
C09.keyboard_action: Learner performs each stage on real instrument, optionally writes own path on paper; do not require DAW, user account, or site input.
C09.guard: These are guide stages, not a graded sequence or an interactive canvas.

C10.title: Week 1 Final Soundscape Map
C10.objective: See one complete mini composition with an independent supporting voice and upper path, hinting at future movement of both.
C10.how_to_read: Native factual source event sequence C01 for recap or C04/C05 appropriately, with clear distinction between exact played pattern and atmospheric metaphor.
C10.keyboard_action: Learner makes and listens to a tiny self-chosen two-voice piece on real synth; ask which line stayed and which changed, then note Week 2 will move the lower line too.
C10.guard: Do not fake completed student work or prescribe an emotional response.

S07.title: Week 2 Two Voices opening
S07.objective: Recognize two separate melodic voices that can meet and change relationship.
S07.how_to_read: Native course heading 'Two Voices', short static roadmap note pair → interval → movement → changed support; no false chord notation.
S07.keyboard_action: Read the two strands as separate voices; play C and E independently, then together, on own keyboard.
S07.guard: Show no on-page musical interactivity, generated lettering or fake keyboard; keep a rich organic illustration composited with continuous native background and substantial teacherly explanatory prose.

D01.objective: See two notes retain individuality while producing a combined musical relationship.
D01.how_to_read: Source C+E dyad, native exact keyboard C/E labels, two separate voice roles.
D01.keyboard_action: Introduce a dyad as two notes at once; play C alone, E alone, then C+E.

D10.objective: Connect two notes, distance, and voice movement.

E01.title: One beginning, five changes
E01.objective: See five different outcomes share exactly the same C+E beginning.
E01.how_to_read: Source FIVE B1-B5 all begin C+E and lead respectively C+F, B+E, D+E, B+F, D+F; they illustrate THREE named categories oblique, contrary, similar, not five distinct motion families.
E01.keyboard_action: Learner plays C+E, tries one different ending, and compares what moved.
E01.guard: No model-generated letters/piano keys, no on-page music interactivity or copied card backgrounds. Precise source labels separate from composable painterly art; prose must teach the graphic in full paragraphs.

E02.title: Oblique: one voice holds
E02.objective: See a held pitch versus another traveling pitch.
E02.how_to_read: Native static source B1 C+E→C+F, B2 C+E→B+E, B3 C+E→D+E as THREE distinct examples. At least two variants showing upper-held versus lower-held where pedagogically useful.
E02.keyboard_action: Explain 'oblique motion': one pitch stays while other moves; on keyboard hold C and move E→F, then hold E and move C→B.
E02.guard: No model-generated letters/piano keys, no on-page music interactivity or copied card backgrounds. Precise source labels separate from composable painterly art; prose must teach the graphic in full paragraphs.

E03.title: Contrary: move apart
E03.objective: Identify opposite-direction movement in two voices.
E03.how_to_read: Source B4 C+E→B+F; B–F end = 6 semitones, diminished fifth/tritone. Exact native keyboard and directional arrows.
E03.keyboard_action: Play C+E then B+F, notice both hands/pitches move in opposite directions.
E03.guard: No model-generated letters/piano keys, no on-page music interactivity or copied card backgrounds. Precise source labels separate from composable painterly art; prose must teach the graphic in full paragraphs.

E04.title: Similar: rise together
E04.objective: Identify both voices moving the same way but by different measured amounts.
E04.how_to_read: Source B5 C+E→D+F: lower +2 semitones, upper +1, ending D–F 3 semitones / minor third. Native exact labels.
E04.keyboard_action: Move C→D and E→F on physical keyboard; compare with contrary case.
E04.guard: No model-generated letters/piano keys, no on-page music interactivity or copied card backgrounds. Precise source labels separate from composable painterly art; prose must teach the graphic in full paragraphs.
